item.title: UAE denies Netanyahu held 'secret' meeting with president during Iran war
item.description: ⁠The ⁠United ​Arab Emirates' ​foreign ministry denied on Wednesday the ​reports ‌of ⁠Israeli Prime Minister ‌Benjamin Netanyahu's visit ⁠to the country, adding such claims are "baseless". The Israeli ​PM’s office said earlier Wednesday ​that Netanyahu had held a "secret" meeting with the UAE president during the Israel-US war with ⁠Iran. Read our liveblog to see how all the day's events unfolded.

item.title: Iran warns US to accept peace plan or risk collapse of Mideast truce
item.description: Iran’s chief negotiator said on Tuesday that Washington must accept Tehran’s latest peace plan or risk the collapse of the Middle East truce, after President Donald Trump warned the ceasefire was near failure. The war, triggered by US-Israeli strikes on Iran more than two months ago, has destabilised the region and rattled global markets.

item.title: In Lebanon, the idea of peace with Israel continues to deeply divide opinion
item.description: In Lebanon, the very idea of peace with Israel continues to deeply divide opinion. As unprecedented negotiations open today in Washington under US mediation, many Lebanese see a chance for a return to stability. But within Hezbollah’s camp, any normalisation with Israel is firmly rejected. FRANCE 24's Serge Berberi and Renee Davis report.

item.title: Israelis chant threats, anti-Palestinian slogans at Jerusalem Day march
item.description: Israeli nationalists swept through the narrow streets of Jerusalem's Old City on Thursday, chanting "Death to Arabs" during the annual Jerusalem Day march, while many Palestinian residents remained barricaded indoors. Every year, tens of thousands of Israelis celebrate what Israeli authorities call the "reunification" of Jerusalem following Israel's annexation of east Jerusalem in the 1967 Arab-Israeli war. item.title: Israeli report says Hamas used 'systematic, widespread' sexual violence in October 7 attack
item.description: A report released on Tuesday by an independent Israeli investigative commission found that sexual violence was a "central component" of Hamas' October 7, 2023 attack on Israel and of the captivity of the hostages that the militant group took back to Gaza.

item.title: London police brace for far-right march and rally marking Palestinian Nakba
item.description: More than 4,000 police officers will be deployed in London Saturday to prevent disorder when a Palestinian solidarity demonstration marking Nakba Day and a far-right rally converge in the heart of the British capital.

item.title: Rights group says M23, Rwandan army commit atrocities in DRC’s Uvira
item.description: M23 rebels and ⁠the Rwandan ​army carried out killings, rapes and abductions during a ​month-long occupation of Uvira in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo in late 2025 and early 2026, Human Rights Watch said ​in ‌a report on Thursday. For more, FRANCE 24’s Georja Calvin Smith is joined by Clémentine de Montjoye, senior Great Lakes researcher at Human Rights Watch.

item.title: Trump touts business wins as China airs Iran, Taiwan concerns
item.description: US President Donald Trump entered his final talks with Xi ​Jinping on Friday touting economic wins that gave markets little to cheer, while Beijing warned Washington about mishandling Taiwan and said its war with Iran should never have started. FRANCE 24's Fraser Jackson reports from Washington DC.

item.title: Price shocks from Iran war power solar sales in energy-hungry Asia
item.description: Soaring costs for fuel due to the Iran war are leading consumers in hard-hit Asia towards rooftop solar power, a likely windfall for China as the world's largest provider of solar technology. FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney speaks with Maria-Eugenia Sanin, Economics Professor at Université Paris-Est Créteil, about reliance on China for renewables. She says that countries "don't need to be independent in the whole value chain".

item.title: Did Israel tip Eurovision 2025 results? NYT report delves into voting data
item.description: As the Eurovision returns, an investigation by the New York Times has revealed how Israel may have influenced voters to help its contestant Yuval Raphael in last year's edition. Story by James Vasina.
